title: The Invitation

beats.narrativeText: An unexpected package arrives containing a letter from Explorer Academy.
Explorer Academy has been observing individuals who show curiosity, persistence and careful observation — and the learner has been selected as a potential Explorer.
The learner reads the invitation carefully to understand what becoming an Explorer will require.

Director Orion explains that before joining permanently, the learner must complete a probationary expedition at Outpost Echo, a long-abandoned research station whose final expedition disappeared from communication many years ago.
The learner must decide how to respond to the invitation and begin an Explorer Journal to record their own observations.
The learner completes their first observation challenge, demonstrating the habits Explorer Academy is looking for.
The learner reflects on what it means to accept the invitation and begin training as an Explorer.
The learner accepts the invitation and sets out for Outpost Echo, unaware of what waits at the abandoned station.

activities.title: Read Invitation
activities.storyContext: A letter from Explorer Academy has arrived, inviting the learner to begin probationary training.
activities.instructions: Read the invitation letter carefully. Notice what Explorer Academy says it is looking for in a future Explorer.
activities.output: A short note of the letter's key points in the Explorer Journal.

activities.title: Create Explorer Journal
activities.storyContext: Every Explorer keeps a journal to record observations throughout their expedition.
activities.instructions: Set up a notebook or sketchbook as your Explorer Journal. Add a title page and your Explorer name.
activities.output: A personal Explorer Journal, ready for the expedition.

activities.title: Record Expectations
activities.storyContext: Before departing for Outpost Echo, Director Orion asks every new recruit to record their expectations.
activities.instructions: Write a few sentences in your Explorer Journal describing what you expect to find at Outpost Echo.
activities.output: A journal entry recording first expectations.

activities.title: Complete First Observation Challenge
activities.storyContext: Atlas sets a simple first task to see how carefully the learner can observe their surroundings.
activities.instructions: Choose an everyday object nearby and record five careful observations about it in your Explorer Journal.
activities.output: Five recorded observations of a chosen object.

activities.title: Design a Personal Explorer Emblem
activities.storyContext: Every Explorer eventually designs a personal emblem to mark their journal and equipment.
activities.instructions: Sketch a personal emblem that represents you as an Explorer.
activities.output: A drawn emblem in the Explorer Journal.

activities.title: Research Famous Explorers
activities.storyContext: Director Orion mentions that Explorer Academy was founded on the work of real explorers throughout history.
activities.instructions: Find out about one real explorer and note three interesting facts about their expeditions.
activities.output: Three facts about a real explorer, recorded in the Explorer Journal.

activities.title: What Makes an Explorer?
activities.storyContext: Not everyone who travels is an Explorer in the Academy's sense of the word.
activities.instructions: Talk with someone else about this question: what makes someone an explorer rather than simply a traveller?
activities.output: None required — this is an open discussion.

prompts: What expectations do you have as you begin your journey to Outpost Echo?

discussionPoints: What do you think Explorer Academy is looking for in an Explorer?
What are you most looking forward to investigating?
parentGuide.preparation: No special preparation required. Have a notebook or sketchbook ready to become the Explorer Journal.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for careful reading of the invitation and thoughtful, specific expectations recorded in the Explorer Journal.

completionCriteria: Explorer Journal created, expectations recorded, and the first observation challenge completed.
